text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST

- Four killed in clashes between Israeli army, Palestinian police. Over 240 Arabs, 12 soldiers wounded in Ramallah, Bethlehem riots. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Paris: Rioting was not spontaneous.
- Comment: A high price for a "hole in the wall".
- Prime Minister promised U.S. President Bill Clinton to ask Congress to release Palestinian Authority funds.
- Israel to allow foreign venture capital funds to operate tax-free.
- Government to study Israel Broadcasting Authority privatisation.
- $390 million in Israel Aircraft Industries guarantees okayed.
- 18 percent drop in summer hotel stays by foreigners. Eilat hoteliers warn deterioration in security would harm winter season.
- Osem to buy Tnuva ice cream plant.
- Israeli contractors to seek other sources of capital for real estate projects at October business conference in New York.
GLOBES
- Dozens wounded in fierce clashes in territories.
- Discounters guilty in shares affairs.
HAARETZ
- Four Palestinians killed and hundreds wounded in protests against the the opening to the tunnel in Jerusalem. Fear in defence establishment of a revival of the intifada in East Jerusalem.
- Comment by Zeev Schiff: Netanyahu consults only with part of the heads of the security establishment.
- Prime minister decides not to cut short his visit to Europe.
- Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon backs accelerating construction of 600 housing units in Golan Heights.
- Editorial: Lighting a match to an inflammable situation.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Fire in the territories.
- Comment Ron Ben-Yishai: The devil is out of the bottle.
- Is the intifada back?
- O.J. Simpson in first interview with Israeli newspaper: "Everyone is looking to hang someone."
MAARIV
- Israel: The tunnel lit the fire.
- Comment by author David Grossman: The intifada will be revived; it's unavoidable.
- Comment by columnist Chemi Shalev: Netanyahu in 100 days has almost completely toppled the new Middle East.
- Editorial: A new intifada?
